note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before the salon opens, what should the receptionist do at the reception area?
options: Rearrange the furniture in a new way each morning
Check it is clean and tidy, with the appointment list ready
Put her own bag and lunch on the desk
Turn the music up loud so passing clients can hear it from outside

questions.stem: Why is the reception area so important to a salon or spa?
options: It is the place where all of the chemical services are carried out
It is the only place where staff are allowed to eat
It is where stock is mixed before each service
It gives the client the first impression of the business

questions.stem: Which is the best appearance for a receptionist in a salon or spa?
options: Clean uniform, neat hair, name badge and a friendly smile
Any clothes she likes, as long as she is on time
Lots of jewellery and strong perfume to impress clients
Her uniform from yesterday, as it is only worn at the desk

questions.stem: A client walks in while the receptionist is on the phone. What should the receptionist do?
options: Turn her back so the client knows she is busy
Hang up on the caller at once, without saying a word to them
Smile and nod to show she has seen her, then help her soon
Ignore the client until the phone call is finished

questions.stem: Which is the best greeting for a client arriving at the salon?
options: "Yes? What do you want?"
"Hold on, I will soon come."
"Hi. Are you here to see somebody, or are you just looking around?"
"Good morning, welcome to Island Glow. How can I help you?"

questions.stem: How soon should a client be greeted after she comes into the salon?
options: After the receptionist finishes her break
As soon as she comes in, or within a few moments
Only when the client speaks first
After about ten minutes, so she can look around

questions.topic: Finding the reason for the visit
questions.stem: Why should the receptionist find out the reason for each person's visit?
options: So she can direct them to the right person or area
So she can decide how much to charge them for coming in
So she can tell other clients about them
So she can keep them waiting longer

questions.topic: Finding the reason for the visit
questions.stem: A client arrives and says she has an appointment. What should the receptionist do first?
options: Take her straight to any free chair in the salon to start
Ask her to pay for the service before she sits down
Check the appointment book or system for her name and time
Tell her the stylist is busy and she must come back

questions.stem: A man comes to the desk and says he is from a supplier and wants to see the owner. What should the receptionist do?
options: Send him straight into the treatment rooms to look for her
Get his name and company, then check if the owner is free
Tell him to go and wait outside in the car park
Give him the owner's home address and phone number

questions.topic: Finding the reason for the visit
questions.stem: A walk-in client (one with no appointment) wants a manicure. What should the receptionist do?
options: Tell her the salon only serves clients who book
Ask a stylist to stop a client's service to do it
Tell her to sit down and wait, without saying how long it will be
Check the book for a free nail technician and time, and offer it

questions.stem: How should the receptionist take a client to her stylist or therapist?
options: Walk with her and introduce her to the stylist by name
Point to the back of the salon and say "Go through there"
Shout across the salon for the stylist to come and get her
Leave her to find her own way to the right station

questions.stem: A first-time client needs to change into a gown for a spa body treatment. What should the staff member do?
options: Ask her to change in the waiting area, behind a towel held up by staff
Tell her to find a place to change by herself
Show her the changing room, the gown and where to keep her things
Give her a used gown from the last client to save washing

questions.stem: The stylist is running 15 minutes late. What should the receptionist do for the waiting client?
options: Nothing, as she will notice the time on the clock herself
Explain the delay, give the likely wait and offer a drink
Tell her the stylist is always late and nothing can be done
Tell her she should go home and come back tomorrow instead

questions.stem: Which of these helps clients feel comfortable in the waiting area?
options: Boxes of new stock stacked on the seats until the stock room is free
A loud TV and staff eating lunch nearby
Dirty cups left on the table from earlier
Clean seats, magazines or a price list, and water or a drink

questions.stem: A client hands you her umbrella and shopping bag as she arrives. What should you do?
options: Put them on the floor by the front door where anyone can reach
Hang them on a hood dryer until she is finished
Keep them safely in the salon's usual place
Give them to another client to hold for her

questions.stem: Why should valuables such as phones and jewellery stay with the client, or be kept somewhere secure?
options: So they are not lost, damaged or stolen during the service
So staff can borrow them while the client is busy
Because the salon must count them for the stock take
So that the client cannot check her phone during the service

questions.stem: Good practice is to answer the salon phone within how many rings?
options: After at least ten rings
Only when the caller rings back a second time
When the receptionist has finished her other work
Within about three rings

questions.stem: Which is the best way to answer the phone at a spa?
options: "Hello? Hello? Speak up, I can't hear you, it is busy here."
"Good afternoon, Blue Mahoe Spa, Keisha speaking. How may I help?"
"Yes, who is this calling, and what is it that you want today?"
"Blue Mahoe. Hold on a minute." (then puts the phone down)

questions.stem: A caller asks for a therapist who is busy with a client. What should the receptionist do?
options: Take the phone into the treatment room so they can speak
Tell the caller to ring again some other time, and hang up
Offer to take a message or ask the therapist to call back
Give the caller the therapist's personal cell number

questions.stem: Which details must a phone message include?
options: Who it is for, the caller, their number, the message and the time
Only the caller's first name, so the message is short and quick
The caller's age, home address and the name of the place she works
What the caller sounded like and how long the call lasted

questions.stem: After you write down a phone message, what should you do with it?
options: Keep it in your pocket until the end of the week
Pin it on the front door for clients to read
Throw it away once you are sure you can remember what it said
Give it to the person it is for as soon as possible

questions.stem: Why should you read a phone message back to the caller?
options: To make the call last longer
To check that you have the details right
Because the caller cannot hear well
So other clients can hear the message too

questions.stem: You need to put a caller on hold. How should you do it?
options: Put the phone down on the desk where they can hear the salon
Say nothing at all and press hold, then serve the clients at the desk
Ask if they mind holding, press hold, and come back to them soon
Ask them to call back later instead

questions.stem: A client who uses a wheelchair arrives for a pedicure. What should the receptionist do?
options: Greet her normally, ask how she would like help, and clear a path
Speak only to the person pushing the chair, not to the client herself
Tell her the salon cannot serve people in wheelchairs
Lift her out of the chair without asking

questions.stem: A client is hard of hearing. How can you help her at reception?
options: Shout loudly so the whole salon can hear
Turn away and speak quickly so she does not feel embarrassed
Speak only to her friend instead of to her
Face her, speak clearly, and write things down if needed

questions.stem: A mother brings a young child who will wait while she has her hair done. What should the receptionist do?
options: Let the child play with the trolley, the hood dryers and the scissors
Ask that the child stays with the parent, away from work areas
Send the child outside to play in the car park alone
Tell the mother that children are never allowed in a salon

questions.stem: A client arrives 30 minutes late for a 1-hour facial. The therapist has another client booked after her. What should the receptionist do?
options: Do the full facial and make the next client wait for an hour
Tell her off in front of the other clients for being late
Explain politely, and offer a shorter service or a new time
Send her away without offering her another appointment

questions.stem: An angry client comes to the desk to complain about her nails. What should the receptionist do first?
options: Stay calm, listen without interrupting, and apologise
Argue back politely to show her that the salon is not at fault
Tell her to stop shouting or leave the salon
Walk away until she calms down by herself

questions.stem: After listening to a complaint she cannot solve herself, what should the receptionist do?
options: Tell the client there is nothing that anyone can do about it
Promise the client a full refund before checking with anyone
Write it down and keep it in a drawer for a few weeks
Pass it to the supervisor and tell the client who will help

questions.stem: Another client asks what service Mrs Campbell is having today. What should the receptionist say?
options: Tell her the service and how much it costs
Show her Mrs Campbell's record card so she can read it herself
Explain politely that she cannot share other clients' details
Tell her to ask the stylist, who will tell her everything

questions.stem: Why should client record cards and the booking screen be kept out of view of other clients?
options: The cards are too untidy for clients to see
They hold private details that must be protected
Clients might book more appointments if they see them
The screen uses less power when it is turned away

questions.stem: A caller says she is a client's sister and asks for the client's phone number. What should you do?
options: Do not give it; offer to pass on a message to the client
Give it to her, because she says that she is a family member
Give it, but only if she sounds friendly
Read out the client's whole record so she can check it

questions.stem: Why should the reception desk never be left empty for long?
options: The phone line will stop working if there is no one sitting near it
Staff will be fined by the government if the desk is empty
Clients are not allowed to sit down without staff
Clients need help, and cash, records and bags could be taken

questions.stem: A stranger walks past reception towards the treatment rooms without speaking. What should the receptionist do?
options: Let them go, as they probably know where they are going
Shout for all the clients and staff to leave the building at once
Politely stop them, ask who they are and how she can help
Lock the front door with them inside

questions.stem: Which of these is a hazard at reception that should be put right at once?
options: A small vase of fresh flowers at the far end of the desk
A bag strap or cable lying across the walkway
A price list on the wall
A box of tissues on the table

questions.stem: A client spills a cup of water on the reception floor. What should you do?
options: Put out a wet floor sign and wipe it up straight away
Leave it to dry by itself as it is only water
Ask the client to clean it up as she spilled it
Put a towel over it and leave it until the salon closes for the night

questions.stem: Why must the area by the fire exit near reception be kept clear?
options: So deliveries can be stacked there in the afternoon
Because clients like to sit near the door to feel the breeze
So the cleaner has space to store the mop
So people can get out quickly and safely in an emergency

questions.stem: Which body language shows a client that you are welcoming and listening?
options: Arms folded and looking at your phone
Looking past her at the door
Eye contact, a smile and an open posture
Tapping your fingers on the desk and sighing loudly

questions.stem: Why should the receptionist use the client's name, such as "Miss Thompson"?
options: It is the only way to find her record card
It makes the client feel known and welcome
It tells other clients who she is
It makes the conversation shorter

questions.stem: A client speaks very fast and you do not catch what she wants. What should you do?
options: Politely ask her to repeat it, then repeat it back to check
Guess what she wants and book the nearest service
Nod and smile as if you understood her
Tell her that she speaks far too fast and must slow down for you

questions.stem: A new client arrives for her first visit. What may the receptionist ask her to do before her service?
options: Pay a fine for being a new client
Clean her own station before she sits
Sign a form saying the salon is never to blame
Fill in a client record or consultation form

questions.stem: Why should the receptionist check that the phone number on a client's record is still correct?
options: So the salon can sell her number to other businesses
So the stylist can call her about personal matters
So the salon can contact her about her bookings
So the number can be printed on the price list

questions.stem: A client arrives for a hair colour. Her record shows that no skin test has been done. What should the receptionist do?
options: Send her straight to the basin, as the test is only a suggestion
Tell the stylist, so a skin test can be done before any colour
Ask the client if she has ever had a rash, and carry on if not
Do the test on her hand at reception and start the colour now

questions.stem: Why should the receptionist not chew gum or eat at the desk?
options: It looks unprofessional and makes her hard to understand
It uses up the time she should spend on her phone
Food is only allowed in the building after the salon closes for the day
Clients will want to have some too

questions.stem: During the day, the fire alarm sounds. What should the receptionist do?
options: Finish booking the client on the phone before doing anything else
Lock the front door so no one can get in
Tell clients to stay seated until the alarm stops
Help clients leave by the nearest safe exit, staying calm

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What number do you call for the police in Jamaica?
What number do you call for the fire brigade or an ambulance in Jamaica?
What is the safe place outside, where everyone meets after leaving the building in a fire, called?
What is the cover called that is put on a client to protect her clothes during a hair or spa service?
What is the small sign worn on a uniform that tells clients the worker's name?
What one word means keeping clients' personal details private and not sharing them?
Which Jamaican law, passed in 2020, protects people's personal information?
What is the pad or book kept by the phone for writing down calls usually called?
What do we call a person who visits the salon to sell a supplier's products to the owner?
What is the part of the salon where clients sit before their service usually called?
When spelling a name on the phone using the phonetic alphabet, what word stands for the letter B?
What type of question, often starting with "how", "what" or "why", lets the client answer in her own words?
What is the word for a client's own things, such as her handbag, phone and coat?
What two words describe taking care of your own body, such as washing, clean teeth and fresh breath?
A client is booked for 10:15 am and arrives at 10:40 am. How many minutes late is she?

essays.stem: Describe how a receptionist prepares the reception and waiting area of a salon or spa before the first client arrives.
essays.modelAnswer: The receptionist arrives early, in a clean uniform with her name badge on. She checks that the desk, the floor, the seats and the windows are clean, and puts away anything that does not belong there. She checks the waiting area: seats wiped, magazines and the price list tidy, and water or drinks ready for clients. She switches on the computer, the till and the phone and checks that they work, and listens to any phone messages left overnight. She prints or reads the appointment list for the day, so that she knows who is coming, at what time and for which service, and tells staff of any early bookings or special needs. She checks for hazards, such as cables or bags in the walkway, and makes sure the fire exit is clear. Finally she puts on soft music and makes sure the area looks welcoming.
markingPoints: Is ready in clean uniform with a name badge
Cleans and tidies the desk and the waiting area, with drinks and the price list ready
Switches on and checks the computer, till and phone, and listens to messages
Reads the day's appointment list and tells staff of special needs
Checks for hazards and keeps the fire exit clear

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would receive a client who arrives for her appointment and direct her to her service.
essays.modelAnswer: I would look up and smile as soon as she comes in, even if I am busy, and greet her politely: "Good morning, welcome to Island Glow." I would ask her name and check her booking in the appointment book or on the system, so I know her service, time and stylist. I would mark her as arrived. If she is new, I would ask her to fill in a client record form. I would offer to take her umbrella or bag and keep it safely, and offer her a seat and a drink. I would let her stylist know she has arrived. If there is a delay, I would tell her how long it will be. When the stylist is ready, I would walk with her to the station or the changing room, introduce her by name and say what service she is booked for.
markingPoints: Greets the client promptly and politely, with a smile
Checks the booking and marks her as arrived; new clients fill in a record form
Looks after her belongings and offers a seat and a drink
Tells the stylist or therapist she has arrived and explains any delay
Walks with her to the right area and introduces her by name

essays.stem: Not everyone who comes to the reception desk is a client. Explain how a receptionist should deal with a walk-in client, a delivery and a sales representative.
essays.modelAnswer: Every visitor is greeted politely and asked how they can be helped, so the receptionist knows the reason for the visit. For a walk-in client, she checks the appointment book for a free staff member who can do the service. If there is a free slot, she offers it and books the client in; if not, she offers the next free time, or a booking on another day, and takes her name and number. For a delivery, she checks that it is for the salon and calls the person who receives stock, so the goods can be checked before anything is signed. She does not let the driver walk through the salon unless he is shown the way. For a sales representative, she takes his name and company, asks him to wait, and checks with the owner or manager whether they can see him now or he should book a time.
markingPoints: Greets every visitor and finds out the reason for the visit
Walk-in: checks the book and offers a free time or the next booking
Delivery: calls the person who checks stock before anything is signed
Sales rep: takes his details and checks with the owner before sending him in
Does not let visitors wander into work areas unaccompanied

essays.stem: Describe how to answer a salon's phone politely and take a clear message for a member of staff who is busy.
essays.modelAnswer: I answer within about three rings, smile as I speak, and say a greeting, the salon's name and my name, for example "Good afternoon, Island Glow Salon, Tashana speaking. How may I help you?" I speak clearly and not too fast. If the caller asks for a stylist who is busy with a client, I explain politely that she is with a client and offer to take a message. On the message pad I write who the message is for, the caller's name, the phone number, the message itself, and the date and time of the call. I ask the caller to spell her name if I am unsure, and I read the details back to check that they are right. I tell her when she can expect a call back, thank her and let her hang up first. Then I give the message to the stylist as soon as she is free, and sign it with my name.
markingPoints: Answers promptly with a greeting, the salon's name and own name
Speaks clearly and politely and offers to take a message
Writes who it is for, caller's name, number, message, date and time
Reads the details back to check them, and spells names if unsure
Passes the message on promptly and signs it

essays.stem: A therapist is running 20 minutes late and her next client is waiting. Explain how the receptionist should look after the waiting client, and why.
essays.modelAnswer: The receptionist should tell the client about the delay as soon as she arrives, rather than leave her wondering. She should apologise and give an honest idea of how long the wait will be. She can offer a choice: to wait, with a seat, a drink and magazines, to come back a little later, or to rebook for another time. If another therapist is free and has the right skills, she can offer that, if the client is happy. While the client waits, the receptionist should check on her every few minutes and give her updates, so she does not feel forgotten. She should also tell the therapist that the client is waiting. When the client goes in, the receptionist thanks her for her patience. This matters because clients who are kept informed and comfortable are much less likely to complain or leave unhappy.
markingPoints: Tells the client about the delay at once and apologises
Gives an honest likely wait time
Offers choices: wait in comfort, come back later, rebook or another therapist
Checks on her and gives updates while she waits
Explains that keeping clients informed keeps them happy and reduces complaints

essays.stem: Explain how a receptionist can help clients with special needs, such as a client who uses a wheelchair, an older client who walks slowly, or a client who does not speak English well.
essays.modelAnswer: The receptionist should treat every client with respect and speak to the client herself, not only to the person with her. She should ask politely what help the client would like, rather than guess. For a client who uses a wheelchair, she makes sure the entrance and walkway are clear, offers to open doors, and checks that the treatment area can be reached; the client may stay in her chair for some services, such as a manicure. For an older client who walks slowly, she walks at the client's pace, offers an arm if wanted, and offers a seat near the desk. For a client who does not speak English well, she speaks slowly and clearly in simple words, uses gestures, the price list or pictures, and writes down times and prices. She should be patient and never make the client feel a nuisance.
markingPoints: Treats each client with respect and speaks to the client herself
Asks what help is wanted instead of guessing
Wheelchair user: clear access, doors and a reachable work area
Older client: walks at her pace, offers an arm and a seat
Language: simple words, gestures, pictures, writes things down, and is patient

essays.stem: An upset client comes to the reception desk and complains loudly about her hair. Describe how the receptionist should handle this.
essays.modelAnswer: The receptionist should stay calm and polite and not take the complaint personally. She should invite the client to a quieter area, if possible, so that other clients are not upset. She listens to the whole complaint without interrupting, nods, and shows she understands. She apologises that the client is unhappy, for example "I am sorry you are not happy with your hair", without arguing or blaming the stylist. She repeats the main points back to check she has understood. If she cannot solve it herself, she explains that she will get the supervisor or manager, and does so straight away, telling the client the name of the person who will help. She does not promise a refund or a free service herself. Afterwards she writes the complaint in the complaint record, with the date, the client's name and what was done.
markingPoints: Stays calm and polite and moves the client to a quieter place if possible
Listens fully without interrupting and shows understanding
Apologises without arguing or blaming
Refers to the supervisor promptly and tells the client who will help
Does not make promises beyond her authority and records the complaint

essays.stem: Explain why a receptionist must keep client information confidential, and give examples of how she does this.
essays.modelAnswer: Client records hold private information, such as names, phone numbers, addresses, medical conditions, allergies, and details of services and payments. Clients trust the salon to keep these details safe, and Jamaica's data protection law requires businesses to protect personal data. If details are shared, a client could be embarrassed, upset or put at risk, and the salon could lose clients and break the law. The receptionist keeps record cards in a closed file or drawer and turns the computer screen away from the waiting area, and locks it when she leaves the desk. She never tells other clients or callers who is booked or what service anyone is having. She does not give out phone numbers or addresses, even to someone who says they are family; she offers to pass on a message instead. She speaks quietly when discussing a client's details at the desk.
markingPoints: Explains that records hold private details, such as contact and medical information
Explains the client's trust, the legal duty and the harm if details are shared
Keeps cards filed and the screen turned away and locked
Does not tell others who is booked or give out contact details, and offers to pass on a message
Speaks quietly about clients' details at the desk

essays.stem: Describe how a receptionist helps to keep the reception area safe and secure during the day, including what she does if the fire alarm sounds.
essays.modelAnswer: During the day, the receptionist keeps the walkways and the fire exit clear of bags, boxes and cables, and puts out a wet floor sign and wipes up spills at once. She reports any broken chair, loose tile or faulty light. She does not leave the desk empty for long; if she must leave, she asks a co-worker to cover, closes the till and locks the computer. She keeps cash, records and clients' belongings out of reach. She greets every visitor and politely stops anyone she does not know from walking into the work areas. She knows the emergency numbers: 110 for fire and ambulance, 119 for police. If the fire alarm sounds, she stays calm, helps clients and visitors out by the nearest safe exit, takes the day's appointment list if it is safe to do so, and goes to the assembly point, where the list is used to check that everyone is out. Nobody goes back inside.
markingPoints: Keeps walkways and exits clear and deals with spills at once
Reports faults and does not leave the desk, cash or records unattended
Greets visitors and stops strangers entering work areas
Knows the emergency numbers (110 fire and ambulance, 119 police)
In a fire alarm: calm evacuation by the nearest exit, takes the appointment list if safe, checks at the assembly point

essays.stem: Explain how a receptionist's personal presentation and communication skills, spoken and unspoken, affect the way clients feel about a salon or spa.
essays.modelAnswer: The receptionist is often the first person a client meets, so she sets the first impression of the whole business. If she is clean, neat, in uniform with her name badge, with tidy hair and good personal hygiene, the client feels the salon is professional and cares about standards. Her spoken communication matters: a warm greeting, using the client's name, a clear and polite voice, and plain words help the client feel welcome and understood. Asking open questions and repeating details back shows she is listening and avoids mistakes. Her unspoken communication, or body language, matters just as much: eye contact, a smile and an open posture make the client feel welcome, while folded arms, looking at a phone or sighing make her feel a nuisance. Good presentation and communication build trust, so clients relax, come back and recommend the salon.
markingPoints: Explains that the receptionist creates the first impression
Neat uniform, name badge and personal hygiene show professionalism
Spoken skills: warm greeting, the client's name, a clear polite voice, plain words
Listening skills: open questions and repeating back
Body language (eye contact, smile, open posture) builds trust and brings clients back

practical1.title: Set up reception, then receive and direct clients in a series of role plays
practical1.brief: As a group, set up the Centre's reception and waiting area as a salon and spa front desk, and then run a series of role plays. First, together, clean and tidy the desk and waiting area, set out the price list and water, and prepare an appointment page for the session. Then take turns: every member works as the receptionist for at least three arrivals, while the others play the visitors and the stylists or therapists, and one member keeps notes. The assessor gives each receptionist scenario cards, for example: a client arriving on time for a relaxer; a walk-in wanting a manicure; a client arriving 30 minutes late for a facial; a client using a wheelchair; a new client who must fill in a record form; a sales representative asking for the owner; a stranger walking towards the treatment rooms. For each arrival, the receptionist greets the visitor, finds the reason for the visit, checks and marks the appointment page, looks after belongings, deals with any delay, and directs or walks the client to the right person and introduces her. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Photos show the desk, the paperwork and people from behind, not faces, unless the person agrees and the Centre allows it. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: The Centre's reception desk, waiting area seats and table
A salon and spa price list, water and cups
An appointment page or the Centre's booking screen for the session
Blank client record forms and a visitors' book
Cleaning cloths, a wet floor sign and pens
photos: The reception and waiting area before setting up
The reception and waiting area ready, with the price list and water set out
The appointment page with each arrival marked
A receptionist looking after a client's belongings in the salon's usual place
A client being walked to and introduced at a station (from behind)
A completed new-client record form and a visitors' book entry
The note-taker's notes for each role play
checklist: Helped clean and set up the reception and waiting area, with no hazards left
Greeted each visitor promptly and politely, with a smile and eye contact
Found the reason for each visit and checked the appointment page correctly
Dealt with a walk-in or late client by offering suitable times
Looked after belongings and explained any delay honestly
Directed or walked the client to the right person and introduced her by name
Dealt with a non-client visitor or stranger politely and safely
Kept other clients' details private throughout
safety: Keep walkways and the fire exit clear of bags, chairs and cables
Wipe up spills at once and use a wet floor sign
When helping a wheelchair user, ask first and never lift a person
Keep cleaning products away from the waiting area once cleaning is done

practical2.title: Telephone and message role plays, and a reception guide poster
practical2.brief: As a group, practise handling the salon and spa phone, and make a one-page reception guide for new staff. Part 1: every member answers at least three calls from callers played by the other members, using scripts from the assessor, for example: a caller asking for a stylist who is busy; a caller asking for a client's phone number; a caller asking about a spa package; a caller with a complaint; a supplier calling about a late delivery. For each call, the member answers with a proper greeting, deals with the call politely, puts the caller on hold correctly if needed, writes a full message on the message pad, reads it back, and passes it to the right person. Part 2: together, make an A3 reception guide poster that shows the greeting for clients and for phone calls, the details every message needs, what must never be shared, how to direct visitors, and the emergency numbers (110 and 119) and assembly point. Each member writes one section. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group.
materials: Two phones, or the Centre's practice phone line, or phones on speaker in separate rooms
A3 card, markers and a ruler for the poster
photos: The phone and message pad set out at the desk
Each member during a call (hands, phone and pad only)
A message being handed to the right person
The poster plan with each member's section
checklist: Answered promptly with a greeting, the salon's name and their own name
Spoke clearly and politely and stayed calm with a difficult caller
Put a caller on hold correctly and came back to them
Wrote complete messages: who for, caller, number, message, date and time
